text:
Alex K: Heads-up: I'm putting together a customer-facing sizing guide for Private/VPC deployments (GPU + network + storage). Want to capture typical workloads + a simple sizing calc so SEs can give quick advice. Draft below, pls comment.

Alex K: TL;DR guidance I want to land on: 1) classify workload (chat, batch embed, rerank), 2) pick model family and quantization target, 3) estimate peak concurrent requests & tokens/request, 4) convert to steady GPU count + burst buffer, 5) add networking/IO headroom and monthly GPU-hours estimate.

Alex K: Example assumptions I'm using for engineers: 
- Chat (interactive): avg response 512 tokens, average 0.7 requests/user/min, 99th-percentile latency target 500ms
- API throughput for 7B-class: ~300-1200 tok/s per A10G (fp16, batching) depending on seq len
- 70B-class: ~60-300 tok/s per A100-40GB (fp16) or H100 faster (H100 ~1.5-2x).

Maria S: Quick Q — do we want to expose tokens/s numbers or translate to requests/s for SEs? Most customers reason in concurrent users.

Alex K: Good point. I'll show both and include a short calculator. Example: concurrent_users * requests_per_minute * avg_tokens_per_request -> tokens/s -> required GPUs = ceil(tokens/s / tokens_per_gpu).

Raj P: Need to call out KV cache sharing for chat history. If customers enable shared KV cache across sessions (lower cold-start cost) it changes GPU throughput assumptions because many requests hit cached prefixes and cost per request drops. Recommend a multiplier: "cold-start factor"=1.0, "warm-cache factor"=0.5.

Leah D: Also add a note about batch sizing and latency SLO tradeoff. For cost-focused customers we can suggest batching windows of 50-200ms to increase GPU utilization. For 70B chat, batching is essential to avoid 4-6x cost compared to small models.

Alex K: Draft calc snippet for SEs (we can ship as a tiny script):
```
# simple capacity calc (python pseudocode)
concurrent_users = 200
req_per_user_per_min = 0.7
avg_tokens = 512
requests_per_sec = concurrent_users * req_per_user_per_min / 60
tokens_per_sec = requests_per_sec * avg_tokens
tokens_per_gpu = 2500  # example for 7B on A10G (depends on seq len)
required_gpus = math.ceil(tokens_per_sec / tokens_per_gpu)
print(required_gpus)
```

Jordan (devx): Can we include a short table of typical tokens_per_gpu values per model+hw+quantization? That's the hardest bit SEs ask for. Maybe three buckets: small (<=13B), medium (13B-33B), large (70B+).

Alex K: Agreed. Proposed bucket defaults (conservative): 
- small(<=13B): A10G fp16 = 2800 tok/s, A10G int8 ~4200 tok/s
- medium(13-33B): A100-40 fp16 = 900 tok/s, A100 int8 ~1400 tok/s
- large(70B+): A100-40 fp16 = 220 tok/s, H100 fp16 = 450 tok/s, H100 int8 ~700 tok/s
(we'll annotate these as variable by seq len and quantization)

Maria S: Remember to call out memory sizing: 70B fp16 needs 60-80GB GPU memory (A100-80/H100 recommended) or model parallel/quantized configs for 40GB cards. That changes node counts + NVLink considerations for on-prem.

Raj P: Networking: For VPC deployments the customer NIC sizing matters. At 1M tok/hr, egress can be non-trivial if they stream outputs. Recommend at least 25Gbps for medium clusters, 100Gbps for large clusters or multi-node model-parallel. Include example formula: network_gbps ~ (avg_output_tokens_per_sec * avg_bytes_per_token * 8) / 1e9. Use 4-6 bytes/token as baseline for UTF-8 compressed.

Leah D: Also call out storage IOPS for model load times. If customers plan to spin up extra nodes quickly (autoscale), they need fast shared storage or local staged snapshots. Recommend NVMe-backed shared storage or cached model store; warn about NFS slowness for 70B cold-checkouts.

Alex K: Seasonal demand note — many customers have 2-3x peaks during promotions. We'll include a "peak multiplier" field in the doc: default 1.5, promotional 2.5-3x. SEs should multiply required_gpus by that for capacity planning/burst pools.

Jordan (devx): Can we provide a sample sizing for a mid-market customer: 25k daily active users, 0.5 requests/user/day (heavy chat), average 300 tokens?

Alex K: Quick calc in-thread: 
- DAU=25k, requests/day = 12.5k -> requests/sec ~= 0.145
- tokens/sec = 0.145 * 300 = 43 tok/s -> trivial, 1 small-GPU handles this. But peak concurrency vs uniform distribution matters. If 10% of activity in 1h window -> window multiplier ~3, tokens/s=130 -> still small. We'll include both the flat and peak windows calculation.

Maria S: Ops + billing note: convert to monthly GPU-hours for contracts. GPU_hours = required_gpus * avg_hours_per_month (720) * peak_multiplier. Add 10-20% buffer for maintenance & failover.

Raj P: Security/VPC specifics: customers can't rely on our cross-region fallback for Private; call out region-local capacity needs and hardware parity (e.g., some regions only have A10G). SEs need a region inventory table.

Alex K: Good call. We'll include a short appendix: hardware availability by cloud/regional sku and recommended fallbacks (e.g., if no A100, recommend H100 or increased counts of A10G with quantization).

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] Draft doc uploaded to Google Drive: https://drive.company.internal/rdw-private-sizing/draft-v1 — please review by EOD Friday.

Leah D: Final comment: Add a short "cost sensitivity" matrix: when to recommend smaller models + prompting strategies vs more infra. E.g., for high-throughput low-complexity tasks, prefer ensemble of 7B with rerank instead of single 70B.

Alex K: Awesome feedback. I'll incorporate and push a first public draft this week. If anyone wants to pair on the tokens_per_gpu benchmarks I have raw perf runs — ping me and I'll share the spreadsheet. :thumbsup:
